request.raw_text: Add circular feature that will act as a attachment for hanging rope. Outer D=4cm and feature has a concentric hole D=2cm. Thickness is 3cm. Feature is touching tangentially vertical surface of the bigger feature of the whistle with its hole and axis is parallel to this surface. Try to centre the feature to the aforementioned surface

areas_to_change.action: Create and attach an annular circular feature with a 40 mm outer diameter, a concentric 20 mm through-hole, and a 30 mm axial thickness.
areas_to_change.reference_geometry: The vertical surface of the larger whistle body feature.
areas_to_change.location: Centered as closely as practical on the selected larger vertical surface, with the annulus outer cylindrical surface tangent to that surface and the annulus axis parallel to the surface.
areas_to_change.description: Add a rope-hanging eye or ring to the larger body region of the whistle. Preserve the concentric opening and join the ring securely to the whistle at the specified tangential interface.

areas_to_preserve.reference_geometry: Existing whistle body and elongated passage/mouthpiece
areas_to_preserve.preservation_rule: Retain their current overall shape, dimensions, orientation, and internal flow path except at the local attachment interface.

areas_to_preserve.reference_geometry: Existing circular opening visible on the end face
areas_to_preserve.preservation_rule: Do not obstruct, resize, relocate, or merge the new rope hole with this existing opening.

areas_to_preserve.reference_geometry: Existing rounded larger body feature, edge fillets, steps, and underside contours
areas_to_preserve.preservation_rule: Preserve all existing contours and blends outside the minimum local area required to attach the new feature.

predicted_final_outcome.geometry: The whistle will include a centered annular lug having a 40 mm outside diameter, 20 mm concentric through-hole, and 30 mm thickness. Its axis will lie parallel to the chosen vertical body surface, and its outside will meet that surface tangentially or through a minimal fused attachment region.
predicted_final_outcome.function: The new hole provides an attachment eye through which a hanging rope, cord, or lanyard can be passed.
predicted_final_outcome.behavior: When securely fused to the body, the annular lug will retain a rope and transfer hanging loads into the larger whistle body without altering the whistle's existing passage.

ambiguities.description: The phrase "vertical surface of the bigger feature" does not uniquely identify one face from the supplied views.
candidate_interpretations: Attach the ring to the broad vertical side face of the large rounded body.
Attach the ring to a vertical end face of the large rounded body.
Attach the ring to the vertical shoulder where the large body transitions into the elongated whistle section.

ambiguities.description: An axis parallel to a planar surface still has multiple possible in-plane directions.
candidate_interpretations: Orient the ring axis horizontally along the whistle width.
Orient the ring axis vertically within the selected surface.
Orient the ring axis along the longitudinal direction of the whistle.

ambiguities.description: Exact tangential contact creates zero-area contact and would not form a mechanically secure, robust single solid.
candidate_interpretations: Fuse the ring with a small controlled overlap into the whistle body while maintaining the intended tangent appearance.
Add a short connecting web or boss between the ring and body.
Model exact tangency as contact only, leaving the ring as a separate touching solid.

ambiguities.description: The requested centering criterion is not fully defined.
candidate_interpretations: Center the ring on the selected face in both available surface directions.
Center it only vertically while placing it near a suitable body edge.
Center it relative to the larger rounded body's bounding box or symmetry planes.
